slots.description:
Three dedicated outdoor pickleball courts at the tennis centre attached to Austin High, just west of downtown on Cesar Chavez. What makes this venue different from every other one in Austin is who else has a claim on it: the City states that "the courts at this facility are shared through an agreement between the City of Austin and Austin Independent School District (AISD)", which is why the opening hours follow the school calendar rather than park hours. Three dedicated courts is a good number for a city where most venues are lines on a shared slab — twenty-one of Austin's sixty courts are dedicated and three of them are here — and the courts are lit during park hours.

That count puts Austin High among the eight Austin venues where at least some courts are pickleball-only rather than lines on a shared slab — twenty-one of the city's sixty courts. It is also one of eleven lit venues, and the only one in the whole directory whose opening hours are set by a school district agreement rather than by a parks department. Of the twenty-one venues published here, this is the one whose availability is least predictable from the outside: everything depends on whether Austin schools are in session.
slots.getting_there: 2001 W. Cesar Chavez, Austin, Texas 78703, which the Census geocoder matched to Austin city, Travis County. It is on the river just west of the centre, which makes it one of the most central venues in this directory's Austin set. As at every Austin venue, the City publishes nothing about parking — a school site with a tennis centre will have some, and that is an expectation rather than a fact.
slots.what_to_expect: Read the calendar before you go. During the school year the courts open to the public on weekday evenings only, from 5:30 p.m. to 10 p.m.; through the summer months they run seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. That is the sharpest seasonal swing of any Austin venue and it follows directly from the AISD sharing agreement — during term the school has the daytime. The courts are lit during park hours, so the evening window is real rather than theoretical. Nothing is published about nets, surface or cost.

faqs.a: Three, and all three are dedicated pickleball courts rather than lines on a multi-purpose slab. The City's entry reads "3 Dedicated Outdoor Courts".

slots.description:
Eight outdoor pickleball courts at Walnut Creek Sports Park in north-east Austin — the largest count in the city by a wide margin, and the only venue in Austin that must be booked. The City marks it "Reservations Required" where every other entry on its pickleball list says Open Play. Eight courts is enough to run a session for thirty-odd players, and it is more than triple the Austin average of just under three. The courts are lit during park hours, and the facility keeps its own hours rather than the standard park schedule: Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., Saturday and Sunday 8:30 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.

Eight courts is 13 per cent of every verified pickleball court in Austin at a single address, and nothing else in the city comes close — Dick Nichols has five and four venues have four. It is the only Austin venue requiring a reservation and, across the ninety-five venues published on this site before Austin, only two others take bookings at all, both of them indoor. Whatever the City charges for that, and it does not say, this is the closest thing Austin has to a purpose-built pickleball facility.

No parking guidance is published, though a sports park of this size will have a lot.
slots.what_to_expect: Book first. This is the one Austin venue where turning up is not the mechanism, and the City does not publish the booking route or the price on its pickleball page — so a call ahead is the honest advice. What you get for that is the best-equipped pickleball facility in the city: eight courts, floodlit, open until 10 p.m. on weekdays. Surface is not stated, nets are not mentioned either way, and no cost appears anywhere on the page.

It is also one of only two published Austin venues in Williamson County rather than Travis, despite sitting inside the Austin city limits. No lighting statement is published for it.

Like North Lake Creek, it sits in Williamson County rather than Travis while remaining inside Austin, which is why neither appears on a county page. Mountain View, four courts a short distance south, is the better option for anything more than a single game.

Because the county comes from the geocoder per venue, this park appears on the Austin city page and on no county page — Williamson's two venues fall below the three-venue threshold.
slots.what_to_expect: Bring a net. Beyond that: one shared slab carrying two courts, open play seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., with no lighting statement to support the evening end of that. On the far edge of the city this is a neighbourhood court rather than a destination, and Mountain View's four courts are the better bet for a group. Surface and cost are not stated.
